analysis: The change is confined to scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py, an offline unittest that statically checks .github/workflows/ci.yml. It adds a PROVIDER_SHARDS constant and reworks test_lanes_are_independent_on_dedicated_supported_mac_runners so each provider shard reads its own route lane (test-provider-N). Only the base text and a truncated patch excerpt were visible, so the full head test body and the matching ci.yml and route changes were not in the supplied evidence. The visible edits only make test assertions stricter or more granular. They add no runtime provider code, no coordinator-to-provider (TB-002) change, no key, attestation, cache (T-041) or App Attest surface, and no new secrets or credentials. The test stays offline. It only reads repository files and runs stubbed subprocesses with temp dirs; the base-side checks already exercise bash with controlled env. No security regression is identified in this file. Open question for integration: whether the corresponding ci.yml change (per-shard route lanes, the runs-on expression, and permissions or sandbox-routing logic) introduces CI trust-boundary issues such as runner routing or secret exposure. That workflow file is outside this batch, so it remains unverified rather than cleared.
